candidates.locator: Page 5, Section part_i, FLOATING SOLIDS OR VISIBLE FOAM
candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of oils, scum, grease and other floating materials that would cause the formation of a visible sheen or visible deposits on the bottom or shoreline, or would damage or impair the normal growth, function or reproduction of human, animal, plant or aquatic life.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a qualitative, non-numeric enforceable discharge prohibition. Interpreting its scope (which materials are covered, what counts as a visible sheen or deposit, and what constitutes impairment) determines whether a numeric limit applies versus a qualitative standard, and whether reported measurements can be compared to a numeric limit at all for this parameter category.

candidates.locator: Page 5, Section part_i, B. REPORTING OF MONITORING RESULTS (MINOR DISCHARGERS)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The minor-discharger classification gates applicability of the entire reporting subsection. Whether the facility qualifies as a minor discharger under this permit changes which monitoring-reporting obligations are treated as applicable for FY2025.

candidates.locator: Page 5, Section part_i, B. REPORTING OF MONITORING RESULTS (MINOR DISCHARGERS)
candidates.exact_span: Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) results shall be electronically reported to EPA per 40 CFR 127.16.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes that DMR submission is a required compliance activity. Interpreting whether electronic DMR reporting was mandatory for a given period (versus waived) affects whether monitoring results were required to be documented and whether absent DMRs represent missing required evidence or a permitted alternative reporting path.

candidates.locator: Page 5, Section part_i, B. REPORTING OF MONITORING RESULTS (MINOR DISCHARGERS)
candidates.exact_span: Until approved for Net DMR, the permittee shall request temporary or emergency waivers from electronic reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a conditional reporting pathway before NetDMR approval. Interpreting NetDMR approval status and whether a valid waiver was in effect changes whether electronic submission was required and how to classify periods with no electronic DMR on file.

candidates.locator: Page 5, Section part_i, B. REPORTING OF MONITORING RESULTS (MINOR DISCHARGERS)
candidates.exact_span: If paper reporting is granted temporarily, the permittee shall submit the original DMR signed and certified as required by Part III.D.11 and all other reports required by Part III.D. to the EPA and copies to NMED as required (See Part III.D.IV of the permit ).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines an alternate compliance pathway when paper reporting is authorized, incorporating Part III.D certification and distribution requirements by reference. Interpreting whether paper reporting was granted, and what Part III.D incorporates, changes which submissions count as satisfying monitoring-documentation obligations and how to treat missing or partial records.

candidates.locator: Page 5, Section part_i, B. REPORTING OF MONITORING RESULTS (MINOR DISCHARGERS)
candidates.exact_span: Monitoring information shall be submitted quarterly. Each quarterly submittal shall include separate forms for each month of the reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets both submission frequency (quarterly) and granularity (separate monthly forms within each quarter). Interpreting this as requiring monthly monitoring data versus quarterly aggregation changes which months in FY2025 are expected to have documented results and whether a missing single month invalidates an entire quarterly submittal.

candidates.locator: Page 5, Section part_i, B. REPORTING OF MONITORING RESULTS (MINOR DISCHARGERS), item 1
candidates.exact_span: Reporting periods shall end on the last day of the months March, June, September, and December.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the calendar boundaries of each reporting period. Different interpretations of which months fall into which period (especially for FY2025 quarters spanning Oct 2024–Sep 2025) change which monitoring intervals are evaluated together and whether evidence for a given month is due under the correct period.

candidates.locator: Page 5, Section part_i, B. REPORTING OF MONITORING RESULTS (MINOR DISCHARGERS), item 2
candidates.exact_span: The permittee is required to submit regular quarterly reports as described above postmarked no later than the 28th day of the month following each reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a hard submission deadline tied to each reporting period. Interpreting the postmark deadline (and which month counts as 'following each reporting period') changes whether late or absent submissions for FY2025 periods are treated as missing required monitoring evidence versus still within a compliance window.
